modifications: Split gate+up: the candidate's two-table kernel with TOPK fixed at 10 and x/y rows addressed by grid z = token * TOPK + slot (only one token admitted). Admission requires exactly QuantizedSwitchLinear (resident) tables, bf16, q4/g64, hidden % 512 == 0, intermediate % 512 != 0 and % 64 == 0.

Served down: omlx's down/combine reproduces MLX's stock gather_qmm + weighted sum; the Flash-Next profile runs mlx2's tile4 fused down instead (fp32 slot sum), so the #4055 idea (fewer rows per threadgroup, more threadgroups) is applied to a copy of tile4's arithmetic. It runs only where the block would dispatch tile4 at width 1 and tile4's own admission accepts; otherwise the down half declines (counted, routed_down_fallbacks) and the block's down runs.

Views: omlx builds them once per plan; mlx2 caches them on the QuantizedSwitchLinear (holding the originals so ids cannot be reused) and rebuilds when an array is replaced. They are applied to every routed kernel, including the #3912 fused-table kernels. The tile4 kernel in qwen4_fused_moe is unchanged (still binds whole tables).
No first-launch self-disable (a kernel error propagates), matching the existing #3912 port.

Live switches for A/Bs: set_expert_views (MLX_QWEN4_MOE_ROUTED_VIEWS, default on) and set_served_down_rows (MLX_QWEN4_MOE_ROUTED_DOWN_ROWS, 2 or 4, default 2). Both are grid/binding-only; the serving kill switch is the policy mode.

Shared fold (mode gate_up_down_shared): gate+up grid z 0 = the shared expert's gate/up rows (qmv_fast 4-bit + SwiGLU), z 1..10 = routed slots; the down launch adds a sixth simdgroup with the shared expert's qmv down rows and ends with mlx2's eager combine: T(tile4 routed) + T(T(sigmoid(g)) * T(shared)), sigmoid with metal::precise::exp as the -fno-fast-math metallib computes it. Unlike omlx, the shared-expert gate logit g is NOT folded: it stays the block's own shared_expert_gate(x) launch and enters the down launch as an input, because an in-kernel 8-bit qmv row differed from MLX by one bf16 ulp on 1 of 36960 full-model calls. Runs at block level only when the block would run tile4, compiled glue is off, the switch holds split resident tables and the shared MLP is plain 4-bit gs64 QuantizedLinear with no lane or tensorfold-prefill hook; otherwise it declines with a counted reason (shared_fold_fallbacks) and the routed half runs as gate_up_down.

2026-10-01 (lane W3, mixed-precision artifacts): the shared fold admits a 4- or 8-bit shared expert (gate/up one width, down its own) with the routed experts still 4-bit. The shared rows read their own namespaced copy of the QMV header at their width (q8f: MLX qmv_fast 8-bit, 8 values per lane per 256-value block, for gate/up at hidden 2560; q8s: plain qmv 8-bit, 4 values per lane per 128-value block plus the guarded tail, for down at inter 640). 4/4 keeps the original kernel source and name byte for byte; other formats get a suffixed kernel (_s88). Admission also requires MLX's own kernel choice (qmv_fast for gate/up, plain qmv for down: not a whole qmv_fast block, not a qmv_quad width). The shared gate logit stays the block's own launch whatever its format (the uncensored artifact's is a dense bf16 [1, 2560] Linear). The MoE row window (qwen4_moe_window.shared_rows) uses the same per-format kernels.

2026-10-01: MoE row windows admit a dense bf16 shared_expert_gate (nn.Linear, no bias): its logit is computed one one-token-shaped call per row (a multi-row dense matmul is not the one-token gemv), recorded as projections:dense_per_row in row-exact windows.
